import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def naive_search_precond (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  haystack.size < 1000000 ∧ 
  needle.size < 1000000
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Character-by-character comparison of `needle` against `haystack` at offset `i`. -/
def isMatchAt (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size) &&
    (List.range needle.size).all (fun j => haystack.getD (i + j) 0 == needle.getD j 0)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def naive_search (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (_ : naive_search_precond haystack needle) : Array Nat :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ((List.range (haystack.size + 1)).filter (isMatchAt haystack needle)).toArray
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition auxiliary definitions
def matches_at (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size ∧
  (∀ j, j < needle.size → haystack.getD (i + j) 0 = needle.getD j 0)

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def naive_search_postcond (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (result : Array Nat) (_ : naive_search_precond haystack needle) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  (∀ i, i < result.size → matches_at haystack needle (result.getD i 0)) ∧
  (∀ i, matches_at haystack needle i → ∃ k, k < result.size ∧ result.getD k 0 = i)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem isMatchAt_iff (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) :
    isMatchAt haystack needle i = true ↔ matches_at haystack needle i := by
  simp [isMatchAt, matches_at, List.all_eq_true]

theorem toArray_size (L : List Nat) : L.toArray.size = L.length := by simp

theorem toArray_getD (L : List Nat) (k : Nat) (hk : k < L.length) :
    L.toArray.getD k 0 = L[k] := by
  simp [Array.getD, hk]

theorem mem_searchList (haystack needle : Array UInt8) (i : Nat) :
    i ∈ (List.range (haystack.size + 1)).filter (isMatchAt haystack needle)
      ↔ matches_at haystack needle i := by
  rw [List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, isMatchAt_iff]
  constructor
  · exact fun h => h.2
  · intro h
    have hb := h.1
    exact ⟨by omega, h⟩
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem naive_search_postcond_satisfied (haystack : Array UInt8) (needle : Array UInt8)
    (h_precond : naive_search_precond haystack needle) :
    naive_search_postcond haystack needle (naive_search haystack needle h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hres : naive_search haystack needle h_precond
      = ((List.range (haystack.size + 1)).filter (isMatchAt haystack needle)).toArray := rfl
  constructor
  · intro i hi
    rw [hres] at hi ⊢
    rw [toArray_size] at hi
    rw [toArray_getD _ i hi]
    exact (mem_searchList haystack needle _).mp (List.getElem_mem hi)
  · intro i hmi
    have hmem := (mem_searchList haystack needle i).mpr hmi
    obtain ⟨k, hk, hkeq⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem.mp hmem
    refine ⟨k, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [hres, toArray_size]; exact hk
    · rw [hres, toArray_getD _ k hk]; exact hkeq
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`LEAN VERIFIED` — the proof compiles with no `sorry`, `axiom`, or other bypasses, using 3 of the 15 allowed compiler checks. Only the four marker regions in `Solution.lean` were changed.

**What I implemented:**

*auxcode* — `isMatchAt haystack needle i`: a bounds check `i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size` conjoined with a character-by-character comparison over `List.range needle.size`, comparing `haystack.getD (i + j) 0` against `needle.getD j 0`.

*code* — `naive_search` filters `isMatchAt` over `List.range (haystack.size + 1)`, i.e. every candidate start position, and converts to `Array Nat`. The `+ 1` matters for completeness: a match with an empty needle can start at `haystack.size` itself, so the search space is `0..haystack.size` inclusive.

*lemma* — three bridging facts:
- `isMatchAt_iff`: the Bool test is equivalent to the `matches_at` proposition (discharged by `simp` with `List.all_eq_true`, which turns the bounded scan into the `∀ j < needle.size` quantifier).
- `toArray_size` / `toArray_getD`: relate `Array.size`/`Array.getD` on `L.toArray` back to `L.length` and `L[k]`.
- `mem_searchList`: `i` is in the filtered list iff `matches_at haystack needle i`. The forward direction is just the filter's predicate; the reverse needs `omega` to derive `i < haystack.size + 1` from `i + needle.size ≤ haystack.size`.

*proof* — `naive_search` unfolds to the filtered list by `rfl`, so both halves reduce to `mem_searchList`. Soundness: the `k`-th element is a member of the list (`List.getElem_mem`), hence a match. Completeness: any match is a member, and `List.mem_iff_getElem` converts that membership into the required index `k`.

This structure sidesteps the nested-loop invariant reasoning the task description anticipates — the inner comparison loop is `List.all`, whose `List.all_eq_true` characterization *is* the inner invariant, and the outer iteration's coverage is `List.mem_filter` rather than a hand-rolled induction. The implementation still performs the required per-position, per-character comparison.
